first.rationale: Current situation shows simultaneous decline in activation (−6% QoQ) and onboarding completion (−4% QoQ), suggesting friction in the early user journey. Memory_31 and memory_86 both demonstrate that simplification directly improves activation and completion, with durable effects. Memory_73 shows promotional pricing is effective for SMB acquisition, but does not address the activation/completion decline driving churn. I am verifying memory_31 and memory_73 because: (1) memory_31 is directly relevant to the observed activation decline and has high consequence, but field-reduction specificity warrants confirmation of methodology and durability; (2) memory_73 is the competing high-confidence option (promotional pricing) and deserves validation of SMB segmentation and revenue sustainability before choosing between activation improvement vs. price response. A standard_experiment on simplified onboarding targets the root cause (completion friction) rather than treating symptoms (competitor pricing), and aligns with primary objective of sustainable qualified revenue. Referral_incentive targets existing customers rather than the acquisition/activation problem. Enterprise_sales_assist does not address SMB segment pressure or activation decline.

final.rationale: Archive verification confirms the critical distinction: memory_31 (signup simplification) delivered +4% qualified revenue with only −1% retention impact, while memory_73 (promotional pricing) shows −12% retention despite +18% short-term revenue—directly contradicting sustainable growth. The current competitive pressure on pricing is real, but responding with aggressive discounting would replicate the retention failure seen in exp_73 and worsen long-term unit economics. Activation and onboarding completion are down 6% and 4% respectively; simplification directly addresses these metrics and has proven durable on SMB segment (our core at-risk population). This preserves the primary objective (sustainable qualified revenue) rather than trading long-term retention for short-term acquisition volume. Activation_messaging is secondary (memory_91 is confirmed but targets engaged users post-activation). Referral_incentive and enterprise_sales_assist do not scale to the urgency of current SMB churn. Standard_experiment allows controlled rollout to validate that prior lift still holds in current market conditions before broad deployment.
